subject: Urgent: CartLane hosted API — p95/p99 spike and tokens/sec collapse
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: support@cartlane.com
Date: 2028-04-24T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Hi Irene,

We just started seeing a sharp regresssion on the Redwood hosted API for our production model at ~09:30 PDT. High-level impact:
- p95 increased from ~0.9s to ~1.9s, p99 peaked at ~2.3s
- token/sec (throughput) dropped ~55% for our typical request mix
- error rate (5xx) up ~8-12% during the window

This started about 09:30 and is ongoing. We rolled no changes on our side. Can you triage and escalate? Our SLAs are at risk and we have a large checkout window starting in two hours.

Attaching a short trace and tokens/sec dump. Please escalate to infra/runtime.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering, CartLane
attachments: cartlane_p95_p99_trace_20280424.json, tokens_per_sec_timeseries.csv

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-24T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Samir — thanks for the alert and attachments. I'm escalating to runtime/oncall (Rishi) and kernel/team (Laura) immediately.
Quick ask while we triage: can you confirm region (us-west-2), model id, and whether you pinned any model variant? If you have a sample request id from the traces that shows the slow p99, paste it here.

We will prioritize a mitigation (routing or rollback) and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

— Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-24T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Adding initial triage notes:
- Confirmed impact on us-west-2 serving clusters for model cartlane-gpt-v2 (quantized int8).
- Timeline shows a deployment of a kernel_selector adjustment at 09:28 that changed preferred kernel to "k8-int8-v2" on the serving fleet.
- Preliminary hypothesis: kernel selection change produced slower kernels for the quantized path (increased per-token compute) and broke a tight scheduling path causing throughput to collapse.

Requesting:
1) the sample request id (from the trace file) so we can pull KV cache and per-token timings.
2) kube host logs from 09:20-10:00 (if you captured them) — you mentioned attachments, thanks.

Immediate mitigation we are evaluating: pin CartLane traffic to the pre-rollout kernel (k8-int8-v1) or route CartLane to the non-quantized fp16 variant for the next 60-120 minutes.

I'm standing by and will update in 15 minutes with a mitigation decision.

— Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: support@cartlane.com
Date: 2028-04-24T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Thanks Rishi — sample request id: 14c9f8e2.
Attached are the kube host logs we pulled, and a CSV of tokens/sec by minute.
Impact notes for our PM/ops:
- Checkout failure rate increased; we saw session timeouts during peak.
- The FP16 variant has higher cost; routing there is acceptable short-term if it restores throughput.

Attachments: kube-host-logs-09-30-10-15.txt, tokens_per_sec_timeseries.csv

Please confirm ETA for mitigation — we need this resolved before the 11:30 checkout window.

Samir

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>
Date: 2028-04-24T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Reproduced and immediate mitigation plan:
- Confirmed that the kernel_selector rollout at 09:28 updated selection weights; quantized int8 requests on several hosts are using k8-int8-v2 which shows ~1.8x per-token latency versus v1 in our microbenchmarks.
- Action A (fast): pin customer routing policy for cartlane-gpt-v2 to kernel k8-int8-v1 at the traffic-router layer. This is a config flip and should be effective within ~5 minutes after the change propagates.
- Action B (backup): route CartLane to cartlane-gpt-v2-fp16 (non-quant variant) for 60-120 minutes while we fully validate k8-int8-v2. Expected cost increase ~25% for that window.
- We'll also publish a temporary telemetry rule to capture per-token timings and kernel id for all requests from CartLane.

I can flip Action A now unless CartLane prefers B. I'll attach the kernel-config-diff and the commands we're running.

— Laura Bennett
Principal Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: kernel-config-diff.patch

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-24T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Samir — sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev-1 for CartLane. Executive summary for your leadership:
- Cause: unintended kernel_selector rollout that favored a new int8 kernel variant (k8-int8-v2) with worse per-token performance for your workload.
- Mitigation: runtime team to pin kernel back to k8-int8-v1 (in progress) and open a short-lived routing to fp16 if required.
- Impact: we estimate 11:00-11:30 PDT to have stability restored; detailed postmortem + remediation plan will follow.

As a commercial gesture given the outage window and the impact to your checkout traffic, we will proactively issue a one-time service credit (details to follow) and prioritize the postmortem. Irene will coordinate the call with your ops and our engineering leadership.

— Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Samir Shah <samir@cartlane.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-24T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spike — hosted API p95/p99 up, TPS down

Samir — quick update and closure for the incident today.
- At 16:50 PDT we applied Action A (pinned kernel selection for cartlane-gpt-v2 to k8-int8-v1). Propagation completed by ~16:56.
- Observed recovery: p95 returned to ~0.95s and p99 to ~1.05s within 6 minutes of propagation; tokens/sec returned to baseline (~+52% from degraded state).
- Error rate dropped back to baseline within ~10 minutes.

Next steps:
1) Full postmortem (ENG-1289) will be published by tomorrow COB with root cause analysis and test coverage requirements for kernel_selector changes.
2) We'll create a safety gating rule that prevents fleet-wide kernel_selector rollouts without a canary in the hosting fleet and an automatic rollback on tokens/sec regressions.
3) Commercial: Marissa will confirm the credit amount and formal paperwork; I'll follow up with a short status call invite.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-1289 (postmortem), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqCartlane-Support-Traces (traces).

Thanks for your patience — please ping if you see any recurrences.
